questions_and_answers.question_text: How is income described in Chinese, as opposed to English?
Write the Chinese for "Her income isn't small."
Write the Chinese for "His income isn't very high."
Write the Chinese for "What do you produce?"
Which adjectives are used with shōurù in Chinese?
Can shēngchǎn refer to both agricultural and industrial production?

answers.answer_text: Yes — it covers agricultural and industrial products, and the operation of a plant.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "agricultural production conditions."

articles.text:
1. A: Zhèi liǎngnián, nǐmende       What has your income been like the
      shōurù zěnmeyàng?              past couple of years?
   B: Zhèi liǎngnián, nóngyè        These past couple of years agricultural
      shēngchǎn qíngkuàng bú cuò,    production conditions have been pretty
      shōurù yě hái hǎo.             good, and income is all right, too.

Notes on No. 1

shōurù: "income, earnings." While in English you say "income" is "large" or "small," in Chinese you say "MUCH" (duō) or "LITTLE" (shǎo).

Tāde shōurù bù shǎo.             Her income isn't small. (lit., "little")
Tāde shōurù bú tài duō.          His income isn't very high.

shēngchǎn: "to produce (agricultural or industrial products), to manufacture; production, operation (of a plant)"

Nǐmen dōu shēngchǎn shénme?      What (all) do you produce?
Yǒu rén shuō xiāngxiàde          Some people say that production and
shēngchǎn hé shēnghuó qíngkuàng  living conditions in the countryside
hǎo yìdiǎn le.                   have gotten somewhat better.
